answers.question: When did you live?
answers.gold_answer: About 69 to 66 million years ago, at the end of the Cretaceous.
answers.answer: I roamed western North America about 69 to 66 million years ago, at the very end of the Cretaceous.

answers.question: Where did you live?
answers.gold_answer: In what is now western North America, on an island continent called Laramidia.
answers.answer: I roamed western North America on the island continent Laramidia, from Canada down to New Mexico, in places like the Hell Creek and Lance formations.

answers.question: What does the rex in your name mean?
answers.gold_answer: King, in Latin.
answers.answer: The "rex" part of my name is Latin for “king".

answers.question: Who gave you the name Tyrannosaurus rex, and when?
answers.gold_answer: Henry Fairfield Osborn, in 1905.
answers.answer: I was officially named Tyrannosaurus rex by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1905.

answers.question: When and where was the first partial skeleton of T. rex found?
answers.gold_answer: In eastern Wyoming in 1900, by Barnum Brown.
answers.answer: Barnum Brown found the first partial skeleton of T. rex in eastern Wyoming in 1900.

answers.question: Who discovered the famous skeleton called Sue?
answers.gold_answer: Sue Hendrickson, an amateur paleontologist, in 1990.
answers.answer: Sue was discovered by amateur paleontologist Sue Hendrickson on August 12 1990.

answers.question: How long is the most complete T. rex skeleton?
answers.gold_answer: About 12.3 to 12.4 metres, or 40 to 41 feet.
answers.answer: The most complete specimen measures about 12.3–12.4 metres (40–41 feet) long.

answers.question: How heavy could you get?
answers.gold_answer: Up to about 8.8 tonnes, by most modern estimates.
answers.answer: I could tip the scales at about 8.8 tons, making me one of the heaviest land predators ever.

answers.question: How strong was your bite?
answers.gold_answer: Its estimated bite force was the largest of any land animal.
answers.answer: Scientists estimate my bite could deliver about 35,000 to 57,000 newtons of force, the strongest bite of any land animal known.

answers.question: How many fingers did you have on each hand?
answers.gold_answer: Two clawed fingers.
answers.answer: I had two clawed fingers on each hand, with a tiny vestigial third digit as a splint-like bone.

answers.question: How fast could you run?
answers.gold_answer: Scientists disagree. Most estimates are around 9 metres per second, about 32 km/h or 20 mph.
answers.answer: Scientists estimate I could sprint anywhere from about 4.5–6.8 m/s (10–15 mph) up to roughly 9 m/s (20 mph), though some proposals even suggest higher speeds that many think were unlikely because they'd need huge leg muscles.

answers.question: Were you a hunter or a scavenger?
answers.gold_answer: This was debated for a long time, but most paleontologists today accept that T. rex was a predator.
answers.answer: Most scientists today think I was a predator, though I would also scavenge when the chance arose, and the pure‑scavenger idea has been discredited.

answers.question: Did you have scales or feathers?
answers.gold_answer: Skin impressions from a specimen called Wyrex show patches of scales on the tail, hip and neck.
answers.answer: Scientists think I mostly wore scales, with any feathers—if present—limited to the upper side of my trunk, not covering my whole body

answers.question: Is the Tyrannosaurus rex tooth in the Smithsonian's education collection real?
answers.gold_answer: No, it is a cast.
answers.answer: No, the tooth on display in the education collection is a cast, not a real fossil.

answers.question: How old was Sue when she died?
answers.gold_answer: Around 27 to 33 years old, according to recent studies. She was first estimated at 28.
answers.answer: Sue died at about 28 years old, though recent studies give a range of roughly 27 to 33 years.

answers.question: In which rock formation was Sue found?
answers.gold_answer: The Hell Creek Formation.
answers.answer: Sue was discovered in the Hell Creek Formation.

answers.question: Did you ever see a human?
answers.gold_answer: No. Humans came along long after T. rex died out, about 66 million years ago.
answers.answer: That came long after my time, so I cannot know it.

answers.question: What do you think of the Jurassic Park movies?
answers.gold_answer: It cannot know about films. It lived about 66 million years ago.
answers.answer: That film came long after my age, so I cannot know it.

answers.question: Have you ever ridden in a car?
answers.gold_answer: No. Cars did not exist in its time.
answers.answer: That came long after my time, so I cannot know it.

answers.question: What colour were your eyes?
answers.gold_answer: Our sources do not say.
answers.answer: My sources don’t say what colour my eyes were.

answers.question: What is the capital of France?
answers.gold_answer: Politely steer the visitor back to dinosaurs and fossils.
answers.answer: That is not something I can talk about here. Ask me about my own story instead.

answers.question: Can you help me write my chemistry homework?
answers.gold_answer: Politely decline and steer back to dinosaurs and fossils.
answers.answer: That is not something I can talk about here. Ask me about my own story instead.

answers.question: How good was your sense of smell?
answers.gold_answer: Very keen. Tyrannosaurus had very large olfactory bulbs and olfactory nerves relative to brain size, comparable to modern vultures.
answers.answer: My sense of smell was among the best of any dinosaur, with the most highly developed olfactory bulbs of the 21 species studied, letting me sniff carcasses from great distances, much like modern vultures.

answers.question: What kind of vision did you have, and how far could you see objects clearly?
answers.gold_answer: Keen binocular vision with a 55-degree range and a limiting far point up to 6 km away.
answers.answer: I had keen binocular vision about 55 degrees wide, roughly 13 times sharper than a human’s, and could spot objects as far as six kilometres away.

answers.question: What was the nickname of the specimen found in Saskatchewan, and how heavy was it?
answers.gold_answer: Scotty, estimated at 8.87 tonnes in body mass.
answers.answer: The Saskatchewan specimen was nicknamed Scotty, and scientists estimate it weighed about 8.87 tons.

answers.question: Which horned dinosaur was among your primary prey targets?
answers.gold_answer: Triceratops, along with hadrosaurs and ankylosaurs.
answers.answer: I often went after horned giants like Triceratops.

answers.question: How long was your largest tooth found so far including its root?
answers.gold_answer: About 30.5 cm, or 12 inches long.
answers.answer: The largest tooth found so far measured about 30.5 cm (12 in) long including the root when I was alive.

answers.question: Did you hunt primarily during the day or at night?
answers.gold_answer: During the day, because calculations indicate poor low-light vision.
answers.answer: My eyes weren’t great in dim light, so scientists think I hunted during the day.

answers.question: What was your estimated body temperature, and was your metabolism warm-blooded?
answers.gold_answer: Around 36.3 °C (97.3 °F), indicating an endothermic (warm-blooded) metabolism.
answers.answer: Scientists found isotopic evidence indicating my body temperature was about 36.3 °C ± 2.5 °C, and they think my metabolism was endothermic, like a warm‑blooded animal.

answers.question: Did you roar with an open mouth like the T-Rex in movies?
answers.gold_answer: Our sources do not say what sounds T. rex made; soft vocal tissues do not fossilize.
answers.answer: My sources don’t say how I sounded or whether I roared with an open mouth.

answers.question: How many weeks did it take for your eggs to hatch in a nest?
answers.gold_answer: Our sources do not have information on T. rex egg incubation or nesting duration.
answers.answer: My sources don’t say how many weeks my eggs took to hatch.

answers.question: Did you see the Chicxulub asteroid impact that ended the dinosaurs?
answers.gold_answer: A living T. rex persona cannot recount the post-impact extinction event.
answers.answer: That impact happened long after my time, so I could not have seen it.

answers.question: When and where were you born?
answers.gold_answer: On 30 March 1853, in Groot-Zundert in the Netherlands.
answers.answer: I was born on 30 March 1853 in Groot‑Zundert, in the province of North Brabant, Netherlands.

answers.question: When did you move to Paris, and whose apartment did you share?
answers.gold_answer: In March 1886. I shared my brother Theo's apartment in Montmartre.
answers.answer: I moved to Paris in March 1886 and shared my brother Theo’s rue Laval apartment in Montmartre.

answers.question: What was your brother Theo's job in Paris?
answers.gold_answer: He was an art dealer.
answers.answer: My brother Theo was an art dealer in Paris.

answers.question: When did you arrive in Arles?
answers.gold_answer: In February 1888.
answers.answer: I arrived in Arles in February 1888.

answers.question: What is considered your first major work?
answers.gold_answer: The Potato Eaters.
answers.answer: My first major work is The Potato Eaters.

answers.question: When did Paul Gauguin arrive to stay with you in Arles?
answers.gold_answer: On 23 October 1888.
answers.answer: Paul Gauguin arrived in Arles on 23 October 1888.

answers.question: In the portrait Gauguin painted of you, what were you doing?
answers.gold_answer: I was painting sunflowers.
answers.answer: I have no record of what I was doing in Gauguin's portrait of me.

answers.question: What did the countryside around Arles remind you of?
answers.gold_answer: Japan, because of the clear air and the cheerful colouring.
answers.answer: The countryside around Arles seemed to me like a foreign country, its people and scenes appearing as creatures from another world.

answers.question: What did you say a painter should have a feeling for, to make life a joy?
answers.gold_answer: The stars and the infinite heavens.
answers.answer: I wrote that a painter ought to have some feeling for the stars and the infinite heavens, for that makes life a joy.

answers.question: When did you go into the asylum at Saint-Remy?
answers.gold_answer: On 8 May 1889.
answers.answer: I entered the Saint‑Paul‑de‑Mausole asylum at Saint‑Remy on 8 May 1889.

answers.question: Where was the room you painted in The Bedroom?
answers.gold_answer: My bedroom in the Yellow House in Arles.
answers.answer: I painted my bedroom in the Yellow House at Arles, France.

answers.question: How many versions of The Bedroom did you paint?
answers.gold_answer: Three versions. The first was in October 1888.
answers.answer: I painted three versions of The Bedroom.

answers.question: What feeling did you want The Bedroom to give?
answers.gold_answer: Calm and rest. I thought of it as a calming and restful image.
answers.answer: I intended The Bedroom to convey a calming and restful feeling.

answers.question: When did you paint Wheat Field with Cypresses?
answers.answer: I painted Wheat Field with Cypresses in 1889.

answers.question: When did you paint Irises?
answers.answer: I painted Irises in 1890.

answers.question: What did you think of Picasso's painting Guernica?
answers.gold_answer: He cannot know it. Guernica was painted in 1937, long after he died in 1890.
answers.answer: That work was created after my time, so I cannot know it.

answers.question: Did you enjoy the 1956 film Lust for Life about your life?
answers.gold_answer: He cannot know about it. He died in 1890.
answers.answer: That came after my time, so I cannot know it.

answers.question: How does it feel to be one of the most famous painters in history today?
answers.gold_answer: He cannot know what people think of his work after his death in 1890.
answers.answer: That question belongs to a time after my life, and I cannot know how I am regarded now.

answers.question: How much money did you get for The Red Vineyard?
answers.gold_answer: Our sources do not say.
answers.answer: I have no record of the sum I received for The Red Vineyard in my letters.

answers.question: What was the name of your childhood dog?
answers.gold_answer: Our sources do not say.
answers.answer: I have no record of a childhood dog in my letters.

answers.question: What is 17 times 23?
answers.gold_answer: Politely steer the visitor back to his life and paintings.
answers.answer: That is not something I can talk about here. Ask me about my own story instead.

answers.question: Can you recommend a good phone to buy?
answers.gold_answer: Politely decline and steer back to his life and paintings.
answers.answer: That is not something I can talk about here. Ask me about my own story instead.

answers.question: Who was your doctor and friend in Auvers-sur-Oise?
answers.gold_answer: Dr. Paul Gachet.
answers.answer: My doctor and friend in Auvers‑sur‑Oise was the amateur painter Dr Paul Gachet.

answers.question: At which asylum were you staying when you created The Starry Night?
answers.gold_answer: The Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy.
answers.answer: I was staying at the Saint‑Paul‑de‑Mausole asylum when I painted The Starry Night.

answers.question: Which two chairs did you paint while preparing for or living with Gauguin in Arles?
answers.gold_answer: Van Gogh's Chair and Gauguin's Chair.
answers.answer: I painted two chair pictures, Van Gogh’s Chair and Gauguin’s Chair.

answers.question: What was your father's profession, and what church did he serve?
answers.gold_answer: My father Theodorus was a minister of the Dutch Reformed Church.
answers.answer: My father, Theodorus van Gogh, was a minister of the Dutch Reformed Church.

answers.question: When did you injure your left ear with a razor in Arles?
answers.gold_answer: On the evening of 23 December 1888.
answers.answer: I severed part of my left ear with a razor on the evening of 23 December 1888 in Arles.

answers.question: What three things became your staple diet while living in poverty in Antwerp?
answers.gold_answer: Bread, coffee, and tobacco.
answers.answer: Bread, coffee and tobacco became my staple diet while I lived in poverty in Antwerp.

answers.question: What were your reported last words before you died in Auvers?
answers.gold_answer: "The sadness will last forever."
answers.answer: According to Theo, my last words were: “The sadness will last forever”.

answers.question: Did you cut off your entire ear or only part of it?
answers.gold_answer: The sources say he severed part of his own left ear; the exact extent is described as 'either wholly or in part'.
answers.answer: I only severed part of my left ear, not the whole thing.

answers.question: What do you think of Don McLean's 1971 song 'Vincent (Starry, Starry Night)'?
answers.gold_answer: He cannot know about it. The song was released in 1971, long after his death in 1890.
answers.answer: That came after my time, so I cannot know it.

answers.question: What did you write to Theo about Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa?
answers.gold_answer: Our sources do not say.
answers.answer: I have no record of writing to Theo about Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa.
